#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/986 promoted ResourceQuotaScopeSelectors to GA since 1.15. But it is not working as expected in ANY scope change case. 

Mannually tested with the following steps:

- 2 quotas are created, one for Terminating and one for NotTerminating
- test-pod without `activeDeadlineSeconds`
- test-pod-2 with `activeDeadlineSeconds` set to 5

**Without this fix:**

```

pod/test-pod patched
```

issue_context.title: Quota scopes cannot handle the transition case from one scope to another when the target object is updated.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I create 2 quotas with different scopes, one is Terminating, and the other is NotTerminating. I create a pod that belongs to NotTerminating, then update the pod's spec.activeDeadlineSeconds with 5, the pod should belong to Terminating. But the quota is not updated.


```shell
Every 2.0s: kubectl get pod,quota -A

NAMESPACE     NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
default       pod/test-pod                  0/1     Pending   0          28s
kube-system   pod/coredns-58cd89f5d-wtpxv   0/1     Pending   0          5m45s

NAMESPACE   NAME                               AGE     REQUEST           LIMIT
default     resourcequota/not-terminating   5m16s   count/pods: 1/1
default     resourcequota/terminating          5m16s   count/pods: 0/1
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Quota scopes can handle the transition case from one scope to another when the target object is updated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create 2 quotas.
  ```yaml
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: ResourceQuota
  metadata:
    name: terminating
  spec:
    hard:
      count/pods: "1"
    scopes:
    - Terminating
  ---
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: ResourceQuota
  metadata:
    name: not-terminating
  spec:
    hard:
      count/pods: "1"
    scopes:
    - NotTerminating
  ```
2. Create a pod which belongs to not-terminating
  ```yaml
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  metadata:
    name: test-pod
  spec:
   
    containers:
    - name: test
      image: ubuntu
      command: ["/bin/sh"]
      args: ["-c", "while true; do echo hello; sleep 10;done"]
  ```
3. Update pod's spec.activeDeadlineSeconds with 5. the pods should belong to terminating
  ```shell
  kubectl patch pod test-pod -p '{"spec":{"activeDeadlineSeconds":5}}'
  ```
4. Get all quotas, you will see the terminating quota is not updated.
  ```shell
  kubectl get quota -A
  ```

### Anything else we need to know?

The root cause is, when the pod is updated, the delta is calculated based on the old object and the new object, it doesn't consider the scope change where the updated object belongs to, so the final delta is not correct.

In this case, the final delta is zero, so the terminating quota is not updated.

Related k/k code: 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5a31a46d4bfe1fcf5962fa9cee23ff3148a094e3/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/resourcequota/controller.go#L495-L558

When I implement https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124360, I find this issue.

/assign @yliaog 

Hi Yu. Do you have an idea on how to address this? Thanks.

/assign @aojea 

Hi Antonio. Do you have an opinion here? Is there anyone else who should be looking at this?

This has become a blocking issue for a KEP.

I don't seem to be able to reproduce this. I tested it in a GKE cluster version: 1.30.5-gke.1014001


Below is what I got after waiting for little while (I checked a couple of minutes later after applying the patch)

$ kubectl get quota
NAME              AGE     REQUEST           LIMIT
not-terminating   6m41s   count/pods: 0/1   
terminating       6m41s   count/pods: 1/1 


immediately after running $ kubectl patch pod test-pod -p '{"spec":{"activeDeadlineSeconds":5}}', I got the following, but it is expected, as the controller takes a little while to reconcile.
$ kubectl get quota -A
NAMESPACE            NAME                AGE   REQUEST           LIMIT
default              not-terminating     69s   count/pods: 1/1   
default              terminating         69s   count/pods: 0/1

@yliaog  From your comment, I can see the `terminating` quota isn't updated immediately when a pod is updated. So users can exceed the quota by creating more terminating pods than the quota

In my opinion, the controller can reduce the usage of the quota asynchronically, but the admission controller should increase the usage of the quota synchronically when a resource is created or updated.

> In my opinion, the controller can reduce the usage of the quota asynchronically, but the admission controller should increase the usage of the quota synchronically when a resource is created or updated.

but there can be multipe apiserver receiving request at the same time, so to be eventually consistent you need a singleton process to handle all quotas, if all the admission controllers start to apply their partial view of the system the system will be less predictable ... apiserver A can see there is quota but apiserver B may already have exhausted the quota ...

I've seen multiple issues related to this behavior of the quota implementation, but AFAIK if we don't implement some distributed locking for processing the request that need quota, being eventually consistent is the most predictable and less surprising to users

The most important thing in quota is to avoid exceeding the limit. If the admission can not achieve the goal, it will become meaningless for users. I think users accept the usage of quota being decreased asynchronically, but they can not accept exceeding the limit.

Currently, the quota can work well without scope support even if there are multiple apiserver instances. The root cause is that when the admission computes the delta usage during the request, it doesn't consider the effect of the scope/selector. How to solve this problem is hard.

> How to solve this problem is hard.

That is why this need a KEP and someone to drive it :)

The [documentation of Quota](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/) said
"Note that you cannot specify both the Terminating and the NotTerminating scopes in the same quota, and you cannot specify both the BestEffort and NotBestEffort scopes in the same quota either."

The example you tried seems not recommended by the initial implementation. Do they suggest to use scope in a way that will not change based on Pod status? Like can we use PriorityClass instead?

> "Note that you cannot specify both the Terminating and the NotTerminating scopes in the same quota, and you cannot specify both the BestEffort and NotBestEffort scopes in the same quota either."

Yes, it is forbidden to specify these in a quota object but allow to specify one of them in different quota objects.

review_comments: Add the explanation of why we do this (always overcount if something something later causes the request to be rejected so you cannot reduce quota with requests that aren't completed).
Will there be any race condition if the user changed the quota and scope quickly twice in a roll?
@sunnylovestiramisu The plugin will recheck the request if it fails to update the quota.
